title: Universal Quantum Raises Over $100 Million Series A
source_used: The Quantum Insider (carrying the Universal Quantum press release); SiliconANGLE for independent confirmation
key_facts: Universal Quantum, a UK-based quantum computing company, announced a Series A round of over $100 million.
The company calls it the largest Series A ever raised by a quantum firm headquartered in the UK.
DCVC and Firgun Ventures co-led; investors include EDBI, Artal, Main Sequence, Hostplus and Roblox founder Dave Baszucki.
The money funds its modular trapped-ion approach, which links many small chips, and its first research centre outside Europe, in Singapore, plus growth in the US, Japan and Hamburg.
It says it is delivering on a $77 million contract with the German Aerospace Center (DLR).
Founded in 2018 by Sebastian Weidt and Winfried Hensinger of the University of Sussex.
quote_evidence: PRESS RELEASE — Universal Quantum, the company building large-scale quantum computing systems for real-world use, today announced it has secured over $100 million in Series A funding – marking the largest Series A ever raised by a quantum firm headquartered in the UK.

Now delivering against a $77 million contract with the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Universal Quantum is establishing a permanent presence via an R&D centre in Singapore, with further international collaborations to be announced soon.
why_it_matters_hint: A UK firm gets large private backing for a modular route to big quantum machines.
notes: Text is a company press release published by The Quantum Insider; SiliconANGLE independently reports the same round. "Largest UK Series A" is the company's claim.
